title: Archive and Orbit
premise: Ada Almeida has spent eleven years as sole caretaker of the Svalbard Deep Seed Vault, running supply runs between Earth and the lunar colonies of two fleets that severed contact after the Reconciliation War. When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, the event is no accident — it is a countdown signal from the vault's hidden reactor, built by the war's architects to force the fleets back to the negotiating table or lose Earth's last living archive. Ada discovers that the ceasefire holding the fleets apart depends on a lie she has unknowingly maintained: a forged transmission claiming Earth's government still exists. To save both the vault and the fragile peace, she must decide whether to let the lie die with the truth, or sacrifice her own memory archive — the recorded life of the family she lost — to keep the fleets from learning the war ended in mutual annihilation. In the end, she broadcasts the truth and her memories together, and the fleets, grieving, choose orbit over war.
about_author: H. M. Zhou is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete agricultural records before turning to fiction. They write quiet, rigorous science fiction about the people who maintain the machinery of memory long after everyone else has moved on.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds of Weightlessness
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. During a routine supply run between Earth and Luna, gravity fails for exactly nine seconds, killing her ship's autopilot and nearly her. She lands shaken, noticing the vault's old reactor dial has moved for the first time in a decade. Emotional beat: unease beneath routine — the sense that the quiet world she tends has a heartbeat.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, flashback woven in. She makes her scheduled delivery to the lunar colony, revealing the two fleets — Concord and Meridian — who share the orbit but not a single word. We learn of her lost family through the memory archive she replays each night. Emotional beat: loneliness as discipline, belonging deferred.

chapters.title: Signals in the Dust
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Back at the vault, she finds the reactor's countdown initiated: 400 days. Buried schematics reveal the vault was never just a seed bank — it is a dead-hand device from the war's final days. Emotional beat: the caretaker discovering the house was always a trap.

chapters.title: The Forged Handshake
chapters.summary: Ada's POV with intercepted transmissions. She decodes fleet traffic and learns both fleets still obey a standing order from 'Earth Command' — a transmission she has unknowingly relayed for years, auto-generated by the vault itself. The ceasefire rests on her relay. Emotional beat: vertigo of complicity.

chapters.title: Meridian's Auditor
chapters.summary: New POV: Ilsa Vann, a Meridian intelligence auditor, notices the nine-second gravity event correlates with a signal origin on Earth — a world officially declared uninhabited. She requests a survey mission. Emotional beat: professional curiosity curdling into suspicion.

chapters.title: Concord's Chaplain
chapters.summary: New POV: Brother Eno, Concord fleet chaplain, receives a private prayer-request from an anonymous sender on Earth — Ada's nightly log, leaking through an old channel. He begins to doubt the fleet's founding grief narrative. Emotional beat: faith tested by a single human voice.

chapters.title: Inventory of the Living
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. She walks the vault's seed corridors, taking inventory, and confronts the reactor's terms: it will fire unless both fleets jointly acknowledge Earth's true status before countdown. She drafts her first deliberate lie to buy time. Emotional beat: tenderness for what she guards, dread of what she must become.

chapters.title: The Survey Vessel
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Meridian's survey ship departs for Earth without Concord's knowledge, violating protocol. Ilsa falsifies the manifest to protect a junior officer she suspects is Concord's spy. Emotional beat: loyalty as a series of small corruptions.

chapters.title: Static Between Sisters
chapters.summary: Eno's POV. Concord command learns of the Meridian launch; hawks push for preemption. Eno argues for contact, citing his mysterious Earth correspondent. He is confined to his quarters. Emotional beat: the cost of speaking truth inside an institution built on grief.

chapters.title: The Visitor
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The Meridian survey ship lands at the vault. Ilsa and Ada meet — the first human contact Ada has had in three years. Ilsa conceals her mission; Ada conceals the reactor. Two liars recognize each other. Emotional beat: wary, aching connection.

chapters.title: What the Vault Remembers
chapters.summary: Alternating Ada/Ilsa POV. Ilsa discovers the reactor and the forged transmission; Ada confesses everything except her plan. Ilsa must choose: report the illegal human presence, or help. Emotional beat: truth as the first intimacy.

chapters.title: The Lie That Holds
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. With Ilsa's help, Ada strengthens the forged Earth Command signal to delay fleet action, buying 200 days. But the fabrication requires her to impersonate her dead mother's voiceprint. Emotional beat: grief weaponized against itself.

chapters.title: Interrogation of a Chaplain
chapters.summary: Eno's POV. Under fleet interrogation, Eno refuses to reveal his correspondent's identity but is released with a tracker. Concord's hawks schedule a strike on Meridian's shipyards, timed before any Earth revelation can destabilize command. Emotional beat: martyrdom reframed as patience.

chapters.title: Orbital Chess
chapters.summary: Ilsa's POV. Ilsa returns to Luna and plays both fleets — feeding Concord's hawks false Meridian positions while preparing a joint-contact proposal. Her junior officer, the spy, catches her. Emotional beat: the spy and the auditor, mirror images.

chapters.title: Countdown at 200
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. The reactor accelerates: the nine-second gravity flicker was its first pulse, and each milestone will shake the system harder. Ada realizes the device isn't a threat — it's a negotiation lever left by the war's losers, and she is its last hand. Emotional beat: inheriting someone else's terrible plan.

chapters.title: The Voiceprint
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, intimate and quiet. To complete the forged transmission, Ada must record a full message in her mother's voice — dredging the memory archive. She almost deletes the archive instead. Emotional beat: the temptation to stop feeling.

chapters.title: Broken Orbit
chapters.summary: Eno and Ilsa POVs interleaved. The strike on the shipyards begins; Eno breaks confinement and broadcasts the existence of a living Earth voice, forcing Concord to stand down mid-assault. Ilsa's spy defects to help him. Emotional beat: chaos as the price of honesty.

chapters.title: Both Fleets at the Door
chapters.summary: Ada's POV. Concord and Meridian ships arrive at Earth together, hostile, demanding the truth. The reactor stands at 40 days. Ada, Ilsa, and Eno meet in the vault's seed hall — the first three-way council since the war. Emotional beat: enemies breathing the same cold air.

chapters.title: The Truth in the Grain
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, climax begins. Ada reveals everything: the forged transmission, the reactor, and the war's real ending — both homeworlds' governments died in the same week, and each fleet has been mourning alone while blaming the other. The fleets' commanders call her a liar. Emotional beat: the loneliest moment — truth told and disbelieved.

chapters.title: Forty Days of Listening
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Ada offers the only proof she has: her memory archive, her family's recorded life, broadcast unencrypted to both fleets. Fleets listen in silence for forty days as the countdown runs. Emotional beat: shared grief as the only common language.

chapters.title: The Choice at Zero
chapters.summary: Climax. At countdown's final hour, the fleets must jointly acknowledge Earth's truth to disarm the reactor — or it fires, destroying the seeds and the lie together. The commanders sign; the reactor powers down; the forged Earth Command signal dies forever. Emotional beat: relief that costs everything false.

chapters.title: Archive and Orbit
chapters.summary: Ada's POV, resolution. A year later, the fleets share Earth's orbit and the vault's work together; Ada remains caretaker, now with visitors, now with her archive public and her grief shared. She plants the first outside seed in eleven years. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not inherited — quiet, earned peace.
